newsitem.title: BELGIUM: W.Europe air passengers up 10.7 pct yr/yr in Feb.
newsitem.headline: W.Europe air passengers up 10.7 pct yr/yr in Feb.

text.p: Passenger traffic on major European airlines grew 10.7 percent year-on-year in February, "a very buoyant market" particularly given the extra day in last year's leap year, the industry association said on Monday.
Removing the effect of last year's February 29, growth this February would have been 3.5 percentage points higher, the Association of European Airlines said in a news statement.

"Taking this into account, the overall 10.7 percent growth for the month indicates a very buoyant market. North and South Atlantic, Eastern and African routes achieved increases in excess of 10 percent," said the AEA, whose 26 members include all of the region's major scheduled carriers.
Aircraft load factors, measures of the seat take-up by fare-paying passengers, also improved.

"February saw improved load factors on all operating regions. The total international figure of 67.4 percent compares with 63.9 percent in February 1996, which itself was the highest February on record," AEA said.
Airfreight markets were more sluggish, with growth pegged at 1.5 percent on last year.
